newsitem.title: USA: DCI buys British co, sees major rev boost.
newsitem.headline: DCI buys British co, sees major rev boost.

text.p: DCI Telecommunications Inc said Tuesday it has definitively agreed to acquire Crossmain Ltd, a privately-owned London-based firm involved in the direct access long distance phone business.
DCI, an international supplier of telecommunication services, said it expects a major revenue increase from the acquisition to begin early in June, with full capacity reached by September.

Based upon current market price, the transaction could equal $15 million, DCI said. It said the deal will be a tax free exchange in which it will exchange a certain number of shares of its common stock for all the stock of Crossmain Ltd. In addition, it said, Crossmain Ltd may earn up to 4,285,714 shares of DCI stock over the next 24 months based upon a formula correlated to quarterly earnings.
It said the acquisition, to be renamed DCI (UK) Ltd, will achieve $24.9 million in sales and $3.7 million in profits in the fiscal year ending March 31, 1998, based on current activity and plans.
Crossmain Ltd is now involved in the direct access long distance phone business in Spain, France, Denmark, Germany, Portugal, Italy and the Czech Republic.
DCI said the operations will continue to expand current lease lines in Barcelona, Madrid, Malaga, Copenhagen, Lisbon and Prague.
"Other strategic opportunities will develop as DCI UK expands its long distance phone operations across Europe with access to the US," DCI said.
